title: Are there any eggs?
grammar: There is / There are; some and any; count nouns
vocab_topic: Food, shopping and things in the classroom
pair_game: Point at a picture. Ask: “Are there any …?” Your partner answers with a number. Then swap!

grammar_box.title: There is / There are
rows: **There is** an egg in the fridge.
**Is there** a book on your desk?
grammar_box.tip: Use any in questions and negatives: Are there any…? There are not any…

questions: Are there any eggs in your kitchen?
How many brothers or sisters do you have?
Do you have any pets at home?
What are some fruits you like to eat?
Are there any books on your desk now?
How many students are in your class?
Do you eat eggs for breakfast?
Are there any cars in front of your house?
Tell me some things you see in your classroom.
starters: Yes, there are … . / No, there are not any.
Yes, I have a … . / No, I do not have any pets.
Yes, there are … books. / No, there are not any.
There are … students in my class.
Yes, I do. / No, I do not. I eat … for breakfast.
Yes, there are … cars. / No, there are not any.
In my classroom there are … , … and … .
samples: Are there any eggs in your kitchen?
Yes, **there are**. **There are** about ten eggs in the fridge. My mother makes eggs for breakfast.
How many students are in your class?
**There are** twenty-four students in my class. Fourteen girls and ten boys.
Tell me some things you see in your classroom.
**There is** a big board and **there are** twelve desks. **There are** some pictures on the wall too.

survey.title: Class survey
survey.question: How many people are there in your family?

game.title: Count and say!
game.rules: Move your counter. Say a true sentence with There is / There are. Wrong sentence? Go back one square!

mini_talk.title: My kitchen and my class
plan: Say what is in your kitchen
Say how many students are in your class
Say what is on your desk
mini_talk.model: In my kitchen **there is** a big table and **there are** four chairs. **There are** some apples and bananas, but **there are not any** oranges. In my class **there are** twenty-two students. On my desk **there is** a notebook and two pens.

cando: say There is and There are correctly
count and describe things around me
